entries.title: I Samuel 26:2
segments: Whatever promises of reformation men may make, unless they are led to hate sin they will continue in some form to commit it; and after temporary and partial reformation, if they go back, they often become worse than before.

entries.title: I Samuel 26:5
segments: No one, when closing his eyes to sleep, can tell to what dangers he may be exposed before he awakes.  Each one should therefore examine and see whether he is prepared for whatever may befall him, and commit himself and all his interests to Jehovah, who alone can make him dwell in safety.

entries.title: I Samuel 26:9
segments: It is never necessary to do wrong in order to obtain any needful good, and confidence in God will lead a man, in the path of duty, to wait till He shall give him what he desires.

entries.title: I Samuel 26:15
segments: Confidence in men for protection and support is always liable to be disappointed, and none are or can be safe except those who put their trust in God.

entries.title: I Samuel 26:19
segments:
Let him accept an offering; if David had sinned, and on that account was persecuted, he would present the proper offering, and thus seek forgiveness and a termination of his distresses. 
 
  Go, serve other gods; by driving him out among the heathen, they had tempted and exposed him to idolatry.

entries.title: I Samuel 26:20
segments:
A flea--a partridge; a thing of small value, difficult to catch, and of little use when caught. 
 
Worldly men often pursue what it is very difficult to obtain, and what, if they should obtain it, would in the end do them little good.

entries.title: I Samuel 26:21
segments: For a man supremely to regard himself and seek his own glory, is foolish as well as wicked.  It exposes him to great vexation, and will end in total disappointment.

entries.title: I Samuel 26:24
segments: Those who seek to glorify God, and to promote the highest good of men, will in the end receive from him all which they can reasonably desire.
